Partial scope remains distinct from every-prime Vinogradov.

Least nonresidue is a prime below p: if composite, both smaller factors are residues and so is their product. With fixed first k primes, modulus 8*product odd q_j handles the supplement for 2 and reciprocity signs: fix the mod8 class first, so p mod4 is fixed; exactly half the nonzero classes at each odd q_j give each sign. CRT then yields precisely 2^-k of reduced classes for every sign pattern.

Fixed-modulus PNT in progressions converts the finite class count to relative natural prime density 2^-k, excluding finitely many p dividing M. Prior plus and final minus signs characterize n_p=q_k; all-plus up to Y characterizes n_p>Y, giving 2^-pi(Y). Each value and each fixed tail have positive density, without an unjustified mean/expectation limit.

For any h(p)->infinity, fix Y first and take limsup_X of the exceptional proportion, bounded by 2^-pi(Y); only afterward let Y->infinity. No growing-modulus PNT is used. This proves density-one subpower bounds, even arbitrary slowly growing h, while allowing an infinite density-zero exceptional set; no uniform all-prime C_epsilon follows.
